enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity. You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Choose Picture B (bottles of alcoholic drinks) and say so.
2. Introduction: link the picture to a personal story, my uncle Tanyi who loved drinking.
3. How the habit started and grew.
4. The consequences: sickness, loss of job, family trouble.
5. The turning point and the lesson about the dangers of alcohol.

**Model composition (454 words)**

Picture B shows many bottles of alcoholic drinks of different shapes and sizes, and it reminded me of the sad story of my uncle, Mr Tanyi, who was ruined by alcohol.

Uncle Tanyi was once a respected teacher in our village. He was tall and smart, and everyone liked him because of his jokes and his kindness. He started drinking at parties, where friends told him that one glass would not hurt him. At first, he only took a bottle of beer on Saturday evenings, but slowly the habit grew. Soon he was passing by the bar every day after school, and the bottles on the shelves, like those in the picture, became his closest friends.

As time passed, the effects became visible. In the morning, he woke up late with a headache and arrived at school with red eyes and a shaking hand. He forgot to prepare his lessons, and sometimes he even fell asleep in class. The parents began to complain, and the headmaster warned him twice. My aunt cried and begged him to stop, but he replied angrily that a man had the right to enjoy himself. At the end of each month, the salary he should have given to his wife for the family was spent on drinks, and the children went to school without books and sometimes without food.

One evening, he drank so much that he could not walk home. He fell into a ditch by the road and spent the whole night there in the cold rain. The next day he had a high fever and a terrible pain in the stomach, and the villagers carried him to the hospital. The doctor examined him and gave him sad news: his liver was badly damaged by alcohol. "If you continue to drink, you will not live long," he said seriously.

Around the same time, the headmaster dismissed him because of his bad behaviour. Uncle Tanyi lost his job, his respect and almost his family, because his wife threatened to return to her parents with the children. That was the turning point. Lying on the hospital bed, he realised that he was destroying himself and those he loved. He promised to stop drinking, and with the help of his church and his family, he kept the promise. Many of his former drinking friends were surprised, and some of them have since followed his example.

Today, my uncle works as a farmer and sometimes speaks to young people about the dangers of alcohol. "A bottle may look beautiful on a shelf," he tells them, "but it can destroy a life." His story taught me that alcohol is a slow poison, and that wise people must know when to say no.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. No clear link with the picture chosen, or not saying which picture is used.
2. Describing the picture line by line instead of building a composition from it.
